title: Brie Souffle
description:
A Brie Soufflé has been one of our most favorite of favorite dishes over the years. It is so luxurious and soothing and delicious and beautiful and easy to make. Wow!
The recipe came from the 1970’s, in The Silver Palate Cookbook, by Julee Rosso and Sheila Lukins. This is a great cookbook and we all got an autographed 25th anniversary copy from Julee when we visited her Bed & Breakfast in Michigan.
This dish is great not only for a special brunch, with Champagne, fresh fruit, and a nice green salad, but also at Easter, with a beautiful ham, and, of course, at great Penn State football tailgates, with everything.
It’s always a treat!
ingredients: 6 tablespoons sweet butter, at room temperature
8 slices of good-quality white bread (we usually use
Pepperidge Farm thin sandwich bread), crusts removed
1 teaspoon salt (or slightly less, says Mommy)
1 dash of Tabasco (or slightly more, says Daddy)
1 pound Brie, softened and without the rind
Butter a 1½-quart soufflé dish or pretty bowl.
Butter one side of the bread slices. Then smear some brie on top.
directions: Cut each slice into halves or thirds, depending on the size of the slices.
Whisk together the milk, salt, Tabasco, and eggs.
Arrange a layer of bread, prepared side up, fitting the pieces together somewhat irregularly. Repeat until you reach near the top.

You may need a few more slices of the prepared bread or may have a few extra, depending on the size of the bowl, how thick you smear the butter and brie on, and how tightly or loosely you assemble the layers.
You could do all this the day before serving and then cover and refrigerate the assembled bowl.
Carefully pour the egg mixture over the bread. Let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until bubbling and golden and beautiful and you can hardly wait to eat it.
